title: Revision: People, Activities & Future Goals
subtitle: A mixed review of personality, physical activities, everyday preferences, and clear future language.

sections.label: Lesson Notes
sections.title: Revision points
sections.intro: This was a revision lesson. It brought together language for describing people, discussing activities and preferences, and talking about future wishes.

cards.title: Describe people with care
cards.text: Use personality adjectives for character, not appearance: friendly, patient, reliable, adventurous, or calm. Give an example to explain your choice.

cards.title: Talk about activities
cards.text: Use play for many team sports, go for activities ending in -ing, and do for many other activities: play volleyball, go swimming, do yoga.

cards.title: Connect a goal to a reason
cards.text: Future language becomes clearer with because: “I’m going to practise more because I want to feel stronger.”

sections.label: Grammar
sections.title: Revision: routine and future
sections.intro: Use present simple for usual preferences and be going to or will for future meaning.

cards.title: Present simple
cards.text: Use it for routines and likes: “She prefers evening exercise.” “They don’t enjoy noisy places.”

cards.title: be going to
cards.text: Use it for a prior intention or plan: “I’m going to join a class next month.”

cards.title: will
cards.text: Use it for an offer, a decision made now, or a general prediction: “I’ll send the details later.”

cards.title: reliable
cards.text: someone you can trust to do what they say

cards.title: outgoing
cards.text: friendly and confident with other people

cards.title: physical activity
cards.text: an activity that moves your body and uses energy

cards.title: team sport
cards.text: a sport played by people working together as a team

cards.title: preference
cards.text: something you like more than another option

questions.q: Which adjective describes someone you can depend on?
Complete: She ___ swimming twice a week.
We arranged the class already. We ___ join next month.

sections.label: Reading
sections.title: A goal with different kinds of progress

readings.title: Choosing an Activity You Can Continue
readings.text:
When people choose a new physical activity, they often begin with a question: Which activity is best? There is no single answer. A good activity is one that fits a person’s interests, schedule, and energy. Some people enjoy team sports because they like working with others. Others prefer a quiet walk, swimming, or an exercise class where they can focus on their own progress.

It is useful to separate ability from preference. A person may be good at a sport but not enjoy it. Another person may be a beginner and still look forward to each session. Enjoyment matters because it makes regular practice more likely. A realistic goal is not “become perfect quickly.” It may be “try one class,” “walk for twenty minutes,” or “learn the basic rules of a game.”

Talking about goals is also good English practice. A learner can say, “I’m going to try volleyball because I want a team activity,” or “I’ll ask a friend to come with me.” The first sentence explains an intention; the second sentence is an offer or decision. Adding a reason makes the message more interesting and easier to understand.

Progress can take different forms. One week, a person may feel more confident speaking to new people. Another week, they may understand a rule more clearly or continue an activity after a difficult day. These small changes are worth noticing. They show that a goal is not only about a final result. It is also about building a routine that a person can continue.

questions.q: What makes an activity a good choice?
opt: It fits the person’s interests, schedule, and energy.
It is the most difficult activity.
It makes regular practice more likely.

questions.q: What does “I’ll ask a friend to come with me” express?
questions.hint: It is a decision made while speaking.

sections.label: Listening
sections.title: Listening follow-up
sections.intro: The lesson included discussion of activities, sport, and future wishes. Use this short listening task with any brief English conversation about hobbies or plans.

cards.title: Listen for preference
cards.text: What does each speaker enjoy or not enjoy? Write one preference using present simple: “The speaker prefers …”

cards.title: Listen for a goal
cards.text: Find one phrase with will or going to. Is it a plan, a decision, or a prediction?

cards.title: Say it your way
cards.text: Make two original sentences: one about an activity you enjoy now and one about a future activity you want to try.

questions.q: Which adjective means “calm and not worried”?
Complete: He ___ basketball with friends on Fridays.
We made the plan yesterday. We ___ start a class next month.
questions.hint: Use be going to for a prior plan.

questions.q: “I can’t find the rules.” “I ___ look for them.”

opt: something you like more than another option
questions.hint: It is about what you like.

questions.q: Which sentence gives a reason for a goal?
opt: I’m going to try yoga because I want to relax.
questions.hint: Look for because and a future plan.

questions.q: According to the reading, progress can include…
